canonical_name: One bit erased
summary: Landauer's principle gives a minimum entropy export per erased bit at room temperature.
source_basis: Representative entropy change for one bit erased near room temperature.

canonical_name: One ideal-gas molecule doubling volume
summary: A single ideal-gas molecule doubling its accessible volume changes entropy by k_B ln 2.
source_basis: Entropy change for one molecule doubling volume.

canonical_name: Protein folding of one molecule
summary: A single protein-folding event involves a tiny but real entropy change.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude entropy change for one protein folding event.

canonical_name: Freeze 1 g of water
summary: Freezing reverses the same magnitude of entropy change as melting.
source_basis: Entropy change magnitude from latent heat of fusion.

canonical_name: Melt 1 g of ice at 0 C
summary: Melting a gram of ice is a clean everyday entropy-change benchmark.
source_basis: Entropy change from latent heat of fusion divided by temperature.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of copper by 1 C
summary: A metal sample gives a much smaller entropy change than the same mass of water.
source_basis: Entropy change from copper heat capacity and a 1 C temperature increase.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of iron by 1 C
summary: Iron is another small entropy-change solid benchmark.
source_basis: Entropy change from iron heat capacity and a 1 C temperature increase.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of air by 1 C
summary: Air has a much smaller entropy change than water for the same mass and temperature change.
source_basis: Entropy change from air heat capacity and a 1 C temperature increase.

canonical_name: One mole ideal gas doubling volume
summary: For a mole of ideal gas, doubling volume changes entropy by R ln 2.
source_basis: Entropy change for one mole of ideal gas doubling volume.

canonical_name: Boil 1 g of water at 100 C
summary: Boiling a gram of water changes entropy by several joules per kelvin.
source_basis: Entropy change from latent heat of vaporization divided by temperature.

canonical_name: Condense 1 g of steam
summary: Condensing steam reverses the same entropy-change scale as boiling.
source_basis: Entropy change magnitude from latent heat of vaporization.

canonical_name: Protein folding of one mole of protein
summary: At macroscopic scale, molecular events become everyday thermodynamic quantities.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude entropy change for a mole of folding events.

canonical_name: Mix 1 mole of ideal gases equally
summary: Equal mixing of one mole of ideal gas is a clean entropy-of-mixing benchmark.
source_basis: Entropy of mixing for an equal binary mixture.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of water by 1 C
summary: Heating a kilogram of water by one degree is a useful everyday entropy reference.
source_basis: Entropy change from heat capacity and a 1 C temperature increase.

canonical_name: Heat 1 kg of water by 1 K
summary: A kilogram of water heated by a kelvin produces a useful entropy benchmark.
source_basis: Approximate entropy change of heating 1 kg water by 1 K near room temperature.

canonical_name: Cool one can of soda by 10 K
summary: Cooling a soda can by ten kelvin changes entropy on the order of tens of joules per kelvin.
source_basis: Representative entropy change for cooling a can-sized drink by 10 K.

canonical_name: Dissolve 1 mole of sodium chloride in water
summary: Dissolving salt in water is a strong everyday entropy example.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude entropy change for salt dissolution in water.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of water by 10 C
summary: A ten-degree change makes the entropy increase much more visible.
source_basis: Entropy change from heat capacity and a 10 C temperature increase.

canonical_name: Freeze 1 kg of water at 0 C
summary: Freezing water mirrors melting with the same magnitude.
source_basis: Entropy change magnitude from latent heat of fusion at 0 C.

canonical_name: Melt 1 kg of ice at 0 C
summary: Melting ice is a classic latent-heat entropy jump.
source_basis: Entropy change from latent heat of fusion at 0 C.

canonical_name: Sublime 1 kg of dry ice
summary: Dry ice sublimation is a large entropy change at a familiar material scale.
source_basis: Entropy change from latent heat of sublimation near the sublimation point.

canonical_name: Evaporate 1 L of water
summary: Evaporating a liter of water exports a surprisingly large amount of entropy.
source_basis: Approximate entropy change for vaporizing one liter of water.

canonical_name: Boil 1 kg of water at 100 C
summary: Boiling water is a much larger entropy jump than melting ice.
source_basis: Entropy change from latent heat of vaporization at 100 C.

canonical_name: Condense 1 kg of steam at 100 C
summary: Condensing steam reverses the large vaporization entropy jump.
source_basis: Entropy change magnitude from latent heat of vaporization at 100 C.

canonical_name: Daily human metabolism
summary: Human metabolism exports entropy continuously as it dissipates energy at body temperature.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude daily metabolic entropy export.

canonical_name: Burn 1 L of gasoline
summary: Combustion on everyday energy scales implies very large entropy exports.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude entropy export from burning one liter of gasoline.

canonical_name: Freeze 1 m^3 of seawater
summary: Phase change at geophysical scales pushes entropy changes into the megajoule-per-kelvin range.
source_basis: Order-of-magnitude entropy change for freezing one cubic meter of seawater.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of water by 1 C
summary: Heating a kilogram of water by one degree is an easy everyday entropy benchmark.
source_basis: Computed from water heat capacity near room temperature.

canonical_name: Warm 1 kg of air by 1 C
summary: Heating air by one degree provides a smaller entropy change than water.
source_basis: Computed from air heat capacity near room temperature.

canonical_name: Melt 1 kg of ice at 0 C
summary: Melting ice at the phase boundary is a strong, familiar entropy jump.
source_basis: Latent heat of fusion divided by the melting temperature.

canonical_name: Boil 1 kg of water at 100 C
summary: Boiling water exports much more entropy than simple warming.
source_basis: Latent heat of vaporization divided by boiling temperature.

canonical_name: Mix 1 mol of nitrogen with 1 mol of oxygen
summary: Ideal-gas mixing provides a clean compositional entropy example.
source_basis: Ideal mixing entropy for two equal one-mole components at equal pressure.

canonical_name: Dissolve 1 mol of sodium chloride
summary: Dissolving salt in water is an everyday entropy-increasing process.
source_basis: Representative order-of-magnitude entropy of solution.
